analyticalQuestion: How do complete-root bounded-variation sampling, the exact integer-lattice cost, observation-coupling growth, and launch retention change the normalized R0.71W-Y triangular-family endpoint envelope?
takeaway: For unit phases and bounded observation coupling, replacing selected-root counting by the complete squared-slope mass changes the exact lattice factor from N M/K_s to M/K_s and the normalized envelope from M^-1 to M^-2. The same upper envelope becomes asymptotically M^-5/6 for eta=M^(1/2) and nonvanishing at eta=M^(6/7); a fixed window can lose launch enstrophy exponentially, while launch-inclusive payment has retention one by definition.
palettePolicy: one muted blue root plus one ochre focus and neutral references
nonColorEncoding: solid, dashed, dotted, and dash-dot lines
filled circles, open squares, open triangles, and open diamonds

panels.A: exact minimum-lattice factor M/K_s and analytic 3/M^2 upper bound
panels.B: bounded-eta complete-root M^-2 envelope against the prior selected-root M^-1 envelope, both normalized by their common M=3 value
panels.C: normalized exact envelope with eta=1, eta=M^(1/2), and eta=M^(6/7), using C_BV(eta)=exp(2 lambda_0 L)(4+C_kappa eta)
panels.D: exact fixed-window heat retention exp(-2 nu d^2 A_0 R^2) against launch-inclusive retention one

dataSufficiency.panelsABC: 30 exact or reconstructed certificate rows on M=2^j+1, j=1,...,30
dataSufficiency.panelD: 32 deterministic integer-R evaluations of the exact heat-retention formula, cross-checked at eight certified dyadic R values
dataSufficiency.fallback: none required; all curves are exact analytic or certificate formulas rather than empirical trends

claimBoundary: Every plotted value is an exact analytic factor, a deterministic extraction of the R0.71Z certificates, or a direct reconstruction of their declared formula. There is no PDE time stepping or DNS. The all-root and floor-free statements apply only to the real-shear, fixed-target triangular Fourier-lattice class with distinct positive integer carriers, unit launch phases, fixed A_0>0, and a mixed window that counts roots on I_t but computes Lambda_1 on the launch-inclusive K_t. The M^(6/7) curve is an upper-envelope diagnostic, not an exact-root construction. The fixed-window heat shear proves failure of automatic launch retention, not failure of every fixed-window atom inequality. No universal endpoint estimate or Navier-Stokes regularity statement is claimed.
